content_text: [1/2 @gregoryblotnick] the best feedback I got on this, from ppl I look up to and respect: "more focus on bond market/fixed income" totally agree. I was trying to straddle the line on "equity analyst focus" but if there's one area to go overboard, its understanding bonds/cap structure will just straight up copy+paste other ppls feedback: -- 1. "the bond mkt is a valuable source of information.. especially if you believe in the wisdom of crowds.. & in case of the bond mkt. the crowd is massive, has lots of capital to deploy & tends to focus on cashflows rather than extrapolating the past" 2. "there are bonds in the stocks - (one can think of what Mauboussin calls the mkt implied forecast period as a form of equity duration)" 3. "monitoring 1 month 25 delta put-call skew & iv rank / percentiles across indicies rates & commodities can be helpful... but what adds value is being able to decompose the move. eg. knowing that if rates move because growth expectations improve equities tend to digest that fine... if a move is due to a "pure" rise in discount rates, then long duration momo and other factors can get absolutely clubbed... (fundamentals can go out of the window if a few big holders decide to have a little trimm.. & all the algos pile on etc.)... knowing what the moves mean and when/why they could matter for equities (& more specifically which factors)... not to trade SOFR or what have you..." -- the most important phrase, in there is understanding the concept of "equity duration" in the context of fixed income duration or how buffett tends to gravitate towards "equity bonds" as investments -- i.e. a consumer staples stock like KO with a bond-ish cash flow stream/return profile its important as an equity investor to understand that you are the most junior tranche, and the 1000 sort of paths to get there and implications...I think in the article I mentioned "understand how distressed debt behaves like equity," u can hit LLMs with that all day, develop a seamless understanding of debt as debt, equity as equity, and the sliding scale up/down a cap structure how those change...when a bond stops trading on yield/YTM is a meaningless #, and represents equity/a call option on recovery...I can't pinpoint "here's how this will help you," but it will. and feedback was consistent on "good work telling ppl to stay the hell out of all the global macro/fx/etc" -- rabbit hole with extremely poor return on time for an equity analyst. for now...classic 1977 buffett article on inflation re: equity investors...good a place as any to start https://6869280.fs1.hubspotusercontent-na1.net/hubfs/6869280/1977%20-%20Warrent%20Buffet%20-%20How%20Inflation%20Swindles%20the%20Equity%20Investor.pdf --- [2/2 @gregoryblotnick] direct quotes from Buffett in there w/ terms to understand -- "The main reason, I believe, is that stocks, in economic substance, are really very similar to bonds." -- "For the moment, let’s think of those companies, not as listed stocks, but as productive enterprises. Let’s also assume that the owners of those enterprises had acquired them at book value. In that case, their own return would have been around 12 percent too. And because the return has been so consistent, it seems reasonable to think of it as an 'equity coupon.'" -- "There is another major difference between the garden variety of bond and our new exotic 12 percent 'equity bond' that comes to the Wall Street costume ball dressed in a stock certificate." etc whole article is a masterclass on bonds/equity/macro and how they all connect if you spend a week just copy+pasting individual sentences from this article into LLM's and asking "explain this like I'm 5," over and over...ditto for most BRK letters...I can't think of an equal Return on Time/Return on Study, thats about as high as it gets. https://6869280.fs1.hubspotusercontent-na1.net/hubfs/6869280/1977%20-%20Warrent%20Buffet%20-%20How%20Inflation%20Swindles%20the%20Equity%20Investor.pdf
